description: AI-produced photoreal explanatory illustration of a low voltage classroom parallel lamp model; not an actual experiment or historical photograph.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: photoreal explanatory photograph for a Korean elementary science magazine and A4 workbook.
Primary request: replace a schematic parallel circuit of three lamps with a convincing real classroom apparatus, precise wiring visible.
Scene: clean white tabletop, softly lit studio product photography, wide landscape 3:1 composition viewed directly from above with a slight elevation so glass bulbs and brass sockets look dimensional.
Subject: at far left one black holder containing exactly two AA cells supplying 3 volts. At center/right exactly three identical small clear incandescent 3V bulbs standing in brass screw sockets on compact white rectangular bases, arranged evenly in one horizontal row. All three filaments glow equally warm gold without obscuring detail.
Electrical layout is essential: one continuous RED insulated supply wire rail runs horizontally above the bulbs; one continuous BLACK insulated return wire rail runs horizontally below them. Holder positive lead joins the red rail at far left; holder negative lead joins the black rail at far left. Each socket has TWO DISTINCT exposed metal screw terminals on opposite sides: each bulb's upper terminal is connected by its own short red vertical branch to the red rail above; each bulb's lower terminal is connected by its own short black vertical branch to the black rail below. The three bulbs thus have three separate parallel branches between the same two rails. Every wire must end at a terminal or an actual small visible joining connector. Show real tidy junctions at all six rail-to-branch joins. Rails end at the third branch. Do not directly connect red rail to black rail anywhere. No branch passes through another bulb. Clearly separated conductors, closed battery-to-bulb-to-battery paths, no floating loose wires.
Materials: clear realistic glass, delicate tungsten filaments, brushed brass screw sockets, visible silver terminal screws, realistic red/black PVC insulation and black plastic battery holder. Gentle shadows on white, sharp detail across all components, very little empty margin. Professional photographic realism, authentic teaching equipment, no diagram symbols, no cartoon, no graphic circles or crosses. No text, labels, logos or watermark. Not a historic photo: a modern low voltage teaching model of parallel lamps. No wall sockets or mains power.
edits:
Edit target: the attached photoreal classroom parallel circuit image. Keep identical composition, white tabletop, black two-AA battery holder at left, three brass sockets with equally glowing clear bulbs, red upper horizontal rail and black lower horizontal rail, existing black branch wiring and photographic realism unchanged.
Make only this essential wiring correction: ALL THREE short RED branch wires must be completely visible and terminate firmly at each socket's LEFT silver screw terminal. Currently the red wires disappear behind/inside the glass bulbs and leave the left terminals disconnected. Reroute each red branch from its upper rail junction slightly LEFT of its bulb, descending in open white space around the left side of the glass, then bending toward and visibly clamping under that socket's LEFT silver screw. Show short metal exposed end under the screw and insulated red wire up to it. The red wire must not enter glass, touch bulb surface, or disappear behind the bulb. Keep each BLACK branch attached to that socket's RIGHT silver screw and lower black rail. Thus each lamp has red on LEFT terminal, black on RIGHT terminal, both visible, separate. Exactly three red branches; exactly three black branches. No extra wires and no connection between red and black rails. This precise contact clarity is critical for a science textbook. No text or watermark.

Remove only the three redundant straight red wire stubs behind glass bulbs. Preserve curved red branches to left screws, all black wires, red rail, three bulbs, battery holder, composition and lighting.
visualReview: Exactly three independent lamp branches between a common red rail and common black rail.
Each red branch visibly meets its own left socket screw; each black branch meets its right screw.
No direct red-black wire connection, serial lamp chain or dangling red stubs.
Two AA cells in one holder are the power source; lamps, not cells, are shown connected in parallel.

prompts.one-cell-preparation: Use case scientific-educational, edit reference photo of one AA battery in holder connected by real red/black wires to a small brass screw bulb socket. Create a sharp high-resolution photoreal classroom product photograph, preserve EXACTLY this single-cell circuit topology and real socket's two distinct terminals, keep all wires connected at the same terminals and all components in the same arrangement. Remove the artificial yellow/green halo and brightness effect entirely; render the bulb as neutral clear glass with no glow. This is a preparation illustration before observing brightness, not an observation result. Remove brand lettering, preserving battery count, terminal spring, holder plastic, metal contacts, plus/minus polarity. Clean white background and soft studio shadows, no sketch symbols, no fake graphic wires, no text or watermark. Every wire endpoint has a physically connected terminal or alligator connector, no stray wire. Keep the original precisely connected closed loop; do not add an extra switch or battery. Crisp materials, true photographic realism.
prompts.one-cell-preparation-final: Edit ONLY the two printed plus and minus symbols on the AA battery: erase BOTH symbols and render a clean unmarked silver/blue battery sleeve. Leave the entire photo unchanged otherwise: holder spring at left, red and black leads, alligator connectors, glass bulb, brass socket, lighting and composition. No letters, branding or polarity symbols anywhere. Do not add any parts.
prompts.series-cells-preparation: Scientific educational photoreal edit of the supplied actual experiment photograph. Preserve its exact topology: two individual single-AA black holders, one bulb with brass socket at top. Far-left holder BLACK lead joins one bulb terminal via red alligator connector; far-left holder RED lead joins far-right holder BLACK lead via the center-bottom alligator connector; far-right holder RED lead joins the other bulb terminal via the far-right alligator connector. This is two cells in SERIES, one closed loop, not parallel. Preserve every connection and component count and orientation from reference. Improve to very sharp large studio photograph on white with realistic metal, PVC wire and clear glass, soft shadows. Remove the original artificial yellow halo and make clear neutral bulb with no glow for preparation before observation. Remove branding and ALL text and plus/minus symbols on battery bodies; battery end caps remain realistic. No extra parts, no schematic lines, no polarity labels, no glow, no watermark. Never alter circuit arrangement.
prompts.parallel-cells-preparation: Scientific educational photoreal edit of supplied actual parallel battery experiment photograph. Preserve EXACTLY reference circuit topology: two single-AA black holders stacked horizontally, both AA cells positive small button end at RIGHT, negative flat end at LEFT spring. Both LEFT black holder leads join together with one side of brass bulb socket via the LEFT red alligator connector. Both RIGHT red holder leads join together with the other bulb terminal via the RIGHT red alligator connector. Thus like battery poles join; one bulb load; two cells connected in PARALLEL. All six wire portions clearly visible with three-way junction at each alligator connector, no plus-to-minus short. Preserve original arrangement. Upgrade into a sharp high resolution studio photograph with realistic insulation, metal socket and clear glass on white. REMOVE artificial yellow halo and show neutral glass bulb without glow, a setup illustration before observing results. No brands, letters, plus/minus symbols or watermark anywhere. Two actual batteries only. Realistic positive button at right and flat negative end at left. Do not change topology or add loose wires.
prompts.series-cell-removed: Precise educational photo edit: remove ONLY the AA battery from the LEFT black holder in this SERIES setup, leaving that black holder completely EMPTY with its coil spring and opposite metal contact visible. Keep right holder and its battery unchanged. Keep every wire and alligator junction EXACTLY where they are with exactly the same connections. Do not bridge the gap in the empty holder with wire or metal. The removed battery should not appear anywhere. Keep bulb neutral clear glass without glow; no brightness result or text. Same white background, photoreal materials, camera and lighting. One full holder and one empty holder only, same series wiring.
prompts.parallel-cell-removed: Precise educational photo edit: remove ONLY the AA battery from the UPPER black holder in this PARALLEL setup, leaving that holder completely EMPTY with coil spring on LEFT and separate metal contact on RIGHT visible. Keep lower holder and its battery unchanged. Keep every red/black wire and alligator three-way junction EXACTLY in place with precisely the same connections. Do not bridge the gap in empty holder. The removed battery should not appear elsewhere. Keep bulb neutral clear glass without glow; no brightness result, no symbols, labels or text. Same white background, camera, lighting and photographic realism. One upper EMPTY holder, one lower full holder only.
prompts.parts-flat-photo:
Use case scientific-educational, photoreal product flat lay. Reference image shows the actual black foam-board star-window lamp kit, used only for material, star-window shape, join tabs and white edge reference. Create a SHARP overhead studio photograph of the kit's SEVEN separate board pieces laid out completely flat on white in ONE horizontal row, all visible, none overlapping: left to right A, B, C, D, E, F1, F2.
Exactly seven pieces with these roles and shapes:
A: rectangular base panel with two long narrow battery-holder mounting areas/slots, NO star window.
B: NARROW long rectangular horizontal internal bulb shelf, one small round hole in its center for socket, NO star window.
C: square top panel, one central EIGHT-point star window.
D: tall rectangular FRONT panel with EIGHT-point star window above center plus one small rectangular switch hole BELOW the star.
E: tall rectangular BACK panel with one central EIGHT-point star window and NO switch hole.
F1 and F2: two identical narrower tall rectangular SIDE panels, each with central EIGHT-point star window, NO switch hole.
Every star has EIGHT triangular points (16 alternating vertices), never five. Real black printed cardstock/foam board with tiny yellow/white speckles, visible white 3mm foam edge, real small interlocking tabs and slots near edges as in reference. Windows are open holes through which white tabletop is visible, no paper filling them. No batteries, sockets, wires, lamp, assembled body, hands or other objects.
Attach a tiny white paper label below each panel with exact single Latin text A, B, C, D, E, F1, F2 respectively; no Korean or other text. Relative spacing seven equal display areas across a landscape3:1 image. Straight overhead view, realistic material microtexture and subtle shadows, convincing photography not illustration, crisp shapes and cuts. Keep all seven separate and countable.
prompts.wiring-five-photo: Create a photoreal overhead educational flat lay, not a drawing. Use reference 1 ONLY for exact electrical topology and placement; reference 2 for the real black battery holders, miniature clear bulb in brass socket, red/black insulated wires and three-terminal rocker switch. Clean white table, all endpoints visible. Two single AA battery holders across top, BOTH COMPLETELY EMPTY: positive flat metal contact LEFT, negative coil spring RIGHT. Do not put batteries or bridge the empty compartments. Bulb socket below LEFT has two distinct screw contacts. Rocker switch below RIGHT has exactly THREE exposed terminals labelled by position: LEFT low, CENTRE common, RIGHT high; switch at centre OFF. Exact FIVE connections: 1 left holder LEFT positive contact to bulb first screw; 2 bulb second screw to switch CENTRE common; 3 left holder RIGHT negative contact to right holder LEFT positive contact, forming one visible junction between holders; 4 branch from that SAME junction to switch LEFT low; 5 right holder RIGHT negative contact to switch RIGHT high. The common terminal is NOT joined to either outside switch terminal in this OFF setup. No extra wires. Real alligator clips can attach to holder external leads, show complete conductor paths without geometric circuit symbols. Clear unlit glass bulb, NO glow. Wires should curve naturally while matching every endpoint of topology reference. Wide landscape image, large apparatus, photographic lighting, readable connection paths; no text other than optional small physical tags 1-5 on wires. Scientifically exact connection is essential.

additional_assets.review: All preparation bulbs unlit; removed cells leave empty compartments; correct series/parallel endpoints; five-wire SPDT centre OFF with empty holders. Generated role images are not measured experiments.
